data.name: Miqdad
data.gender_notes: Miqdad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Miqdad was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and one of the earliest converts to Islam. The name symbolizes loyalty, courage, and devotion. The name Miqdad carries the meaning “Companion of the Prophet” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Miqdad usually hope their child will grow to embody companion of the prophet and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Miqdad bin Aswad was a renowned Sahabi who fought alongside the Prophet in several battles and was known for his bravery and unwavering faith.
data.etymology: Miqdad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Companion of the Prophet.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Miqdad total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Miqdad was a prominent companion of Prophet Muhammad (p.b.u.h.) who was known for his unwavering loyalty, bravery, and courage. He was amongst the first Muslims in Makkah and played a crucial role in the early days of Islam by providing shelter to many companions and disguising their religious practices from the hostile Makkans. The name "Miqdad" carries the legacy of a proud and loyal follower of Islam who stood firm in his belief, inspiring generations to come.
data.spiritual_significance: The soul-stirring tale of Miqdad teaches us the values of unwavering faith, bravery, and loyalty. In a spiritual sense, the name serves as a reminder to remain committed to our beliefs and continue to strive towards the path of truth, even in the face of adversity. It inspires us to be like Miqdad, faithfully following the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (p.b.u.h.) and embodying the noble qualities of a true Muslim. The name spiritual significance highlights the significance of staying committed to our faith, a reminder that our actions and beliefs can have a profound impact on ourselves, our families, and our communities.
